topic.angle: Same deposit, more years of compounding

panels.text: Ana puts $5,000 into an account at 25. Ben puts $5,000 into an identical one at 45. Both leave it alone until 65.
Compound interest means interest is added to the balance, and then that bigger balance earns interest too.
Assume 7% a year, an example number, not a forecast. Ben's $5,000 has 20 years to grow and reaches about $19,300.
Ana's has 40 years and reaches about $74,900.
The twist: twenty extra years didn't double her result. They multiplied it by almost 4, because each year's growth builds on all the growth before it.

probes.question: True or false: with compound interest, interest earned also earns interest.
About how many times bigger does a balance grow with 20 extra years at 7% a year?

claims.claim: Compound interest: interest accumulated on principal and previous interest (panel 2, probe 1)
claims.quote: Compound interest or anatocism is interest accumulated from a principal sum and previously accumulated interest.

claims.claim: Ages 25/45 to 65 give 40 and 20 years; extra 20 years multiplies result by almost 4 (not double) (probe 2)
